ANA and NYR enter tonight's game at Madison Square Garden close together. Both teams generate 3.21 expected goals per 60 minutes (a measure of chance quality), but NYR gives up fewer, 2.87 to ANA's 3.32. At five on five, ANA has taken 47% of the expected goals in its games and NYR 51%. On special teams, NYR holds the edge on the penalty kill (0.51 expected goals allowed per game to ANA's 0.69) and slightly on the power play (0.73 to 0.69), though NYR takes 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays. The model has it nearly even: 3.15 expected goals for NYR, 2.99 for ANA.

The goalie matchup favors the home side this season. Projected starter Dylan Garand (NYR) is at 2.9 goals saved above expected (how many goals he has stopped beyond what the shot quality predicted), with a .927 save percentage, and Igor Shesterkin is on injured reserve. Projected ANA starter Ville Husso is at 1.47 across two games, and last season he was at minus 2.37 over 20 games. Husso starts over Lukas Dostal, who has 6 of 7 starts. Recent form is mixed. ANA is 2-3-0 in its last five but held 52% of the expected goals in those games, while NYR is 2-2-1 with 48%.

Among players to watch, Alexis Lafrenière (NYR) has a 34% chance to score and is flagged as a breakout who is due to cool. Beckett Sennecke (ANA) also sits at 34%. Mika Zibanejad (NYR) has a 68% chance of a point and runs the top power play, while Leo Carlsson (ANA) is at 72%. Mikael Granlund could return for ANA after coming off the out list, now day-to-day, with a 6-game point streak.
